scores.evidence: There are three can-do objectives: o1 apply 「設定を書ける」, o2 understand 「説明できる」 and o3 evaluate 「判断できる」. Each is assessed by 3 or more questions with an objectiveId: o1 by q0, q1, q2 and q5; o2 by q3, q6 and q7; o3 by q4, q9 and q8. q1 and q5 are apply items, q2 is analyze, and q8 and q9 are evaluate.

hook-problem states a concrete failure in 2 sentences: 「CLAUDE.mdに「`.env` は編集しないこと」と書いたのに、Claudeが `.env` を書き換えようとしました。」. A version line follows it. hook-predict is an ungraded predict quiz with real near-misses: 「太字で「絶対に」」, the per-request reminder, and Manual mode. Its explanation leads straight into the lesson (「このレッスンでは、その仕組みのひとつ、フックを作ります。」).

The prerequisites name 第2回, 第6回 and 第7回, plus jq and JSON editing, and s2-setup starts with `jq --version`. s1-lead recalls 「第6回のとおり」 and s5-lead recalls 「第7回のスキルやサブエージェントは」. Each segment defines its new terms in a definitions block before using them, with the same wording as the glossary (s1-defs, s2-defs, s4-defs, s5-defs). エージェントループ and リンター（linter） were taught in cc-01 and cc-04. The only small gap is the unglossed `onFailure` in s3-pitfall (see niceToHave).

measure.mjs prints 「prose 1897 (budget 1,200–2,400) · read 2883 · practice reading 1249 · questions 10 · practice sections 1 · est 17.8 min (must be ≤ 20; estMinutes 18)」, and estMinutes 18 is the rounded estimate. lint --strict reports 0 warnings, and no segment adds more than 3 new terms (s4: MCP, MCPサーバー, スコープ). Each screen breaks the text with a table, a code block, a diagram or a check.

s2 is a full worked example: the script, its registration, then 3 steps with subgoal titles (「① スクリプトを書く」「② 実行を許可して登録する」「③ 予想してから、手で試す」). Each step says why (「`exit 2` は「止める」の合図で…」) and gives an expect and a troubleshoot. The practice then fades it (「例題と違うのは、マッチャーと取り出す項目です。」) with the same JSON test layout (p-predict hint), and part 2 is an independent evaluation.

There are inline checks in s1, s2, s3, s5 and the practice, so no two content sections in a row go without one (s4 sits between the s3 and s5 checks). They include q1, an apply item (choose PostToolUse for 「編集したら、毎回そのテストを実行する」), and q2, an analyze item (`cd docs && rm notes.txt` is not blocked; `rmdir old` is). Every wrong option has feedback. q4 is close to recognition right after s5-pitfall (see niceToHave).

All six misconceptions in the brief are named and corrected with a reason. (1) CLAUDE.md as a guarantee: q0 a/b, q7 b. (2) 「`exit 1` で止まる」: s3-pitfall, q3 a, q5 b. (3) 「`exit 0` は許可」: s3-zero 「止めないだけで、許可ではありません」, q3 d. (4) PostToolUse undo: q6 b. (5) The condition covers everything: q2 d 「条件は、書いた文字の並びだけを見ています」 and the practice-prompt note on Bash writes. (6) Official means safe: q4 d, q8 b, q9 b/d. Each feedback is 2 sentences or fewer.

s1-lifecycle is a process diagram with 6 nodes. Its labels use the text's terms (PreToolUse, PostToolUse and Stop フック; 「通す（権限の確認へ）」 matches s3-table). The caption gives the takeaway (「PreToolUseフックは、ツールの実行を止められます。」), and the alt describes both paths. Every table has 2 columns and a caption, and there are no decorative images.

The task is authentic: protect `.env` with a PreToolUse hook, predict, test by hand, then confirm through Claude with practice-prompt. The help comes in layers: step hints, then troubleshoot, then the model answer (practice-model-script and practice-model-settings). Part 2 is a transfer evaluation of two fictional candidates, with model write-ups placed after q9. practice-checklist gives 5 observable success criteria (「cat .envで、中身が変わっていないことを確かめました」).

summary-points has 4 points and comes after the exam. summary-next opens with a reflection prompt (「あなたのCLAUDE.mdで、本当は毎回必ず守らせたいルールはどれでしょう？」), links the Japanese hooks guide and names 「第9回｜並列で進める・自動で回す」. summary-cards has 7 flashcards, and askTutor offers 3 follow-ups.

All 5 findings in audit-cc-08-hooks-mcp.json are already in the text: 「ふつう」 plus the `onFailure` exception in s3-pitfall and card-exit1, q6 limited to PostToolUse and stating stderr, 「処理（ここではコマンド）」 in s1-config, and the `/hooks` expect without the matcher. hook-problem pins the version to v2.1.304. Non-obvious claims cite official pages: 「AnthropicはMCPサーバーを監査していません」 cites cc-security, and the scopes cite cc-mcp. The brief records that the scripts and test commands were run.

The lesson keeps です・ます and a warm tone throughout (「詰まったら、次の模範解答と比べます。」「予想してから、手で試す」), with no banned phrases. Terms stay consistent: 「権限の確認」「標準エラー出力」「拒否ルール」. Some phrasing still reads translated or clipped, such as 「止めないエラー」 (non-blocking error) and 「ネット越しのサーバー」 in s4-add. The ja-editor owns these.

jp is the only declared locale and it is complete. The diagram labels are Japanese, s1-lifecycle has a descriptive alt, and every table has a caption. The link text in summary-next is descriptive (「フックの公式ガイド（日本語）」). No text is baked into images.

niceToHave: s5-check q4: option a is the only option about what the plugin contains, and s5-pitfall has just said 「中身は自分で確かめます」, so the item is close to recognition. Replace option b with a content-related distractor so the item tests priority: md 「READMEの機能説明が、自分の使い方に合っているか」, feedback 「機能の説明は、中で何が動くかを教えてくれません。`hooks/hooks.json` や `.mcp.json` で、実行されるものを確かめます。」.

s4 / summary-points[2]: the `claude mcp add` commands and the three scopes are taught and summarised (「MCPサーバーは `claude mcp add` で追加し、スコープを選びます。」), but no objective names them and only card-scopes and a q8 distractor touch them. Either reframe the summary point toward o3 (for example 「MCPサーバーは、スコープで使える範囲が決まります。`project` はチーム全員に効くので、入れる前に確かめます。」) or add a short inline check in s4 tied to o3, such as which scope shares a server with the team.
s3-pitfall: `onFailure` appears without a gloss, yet q3's stem relies on it (「`onFailure` は設定していません」). Suggested text: 「フックの設定項目 `onFailure` を `"block"` にしたフックなどでは、失敗でも止まります。」

factual doubt: facts-cc-08-hooks-mcp.md (Missed items, safety) says that without managed settings or a Team/Enterprise login, a plugin mod can approve a call that a PreToolUse hook blocked. s3-zero (「`exit 2` は、どの権限モードでも操作を止めます」) is still true as written, because it is about permission modes. Still, a one-line mention in s5-risk would strengthen o3, for example 「プラグインに含まれるモッド（mod）は、フックが止めた操作を許可できる場合もあります。」 with cite cc-plugin-security. Check the exact wording against the mods page first.

s2-lead: only ex-register says the hands-on part is for macOS/Linux (「macOSとLinuxでは」). Stating the environment up front would save Windows learners a dead end, for example 「macOS・Linux（WSLを含む）のbashで進めます。」.

check-quiz q7: answer a (「フックが、Claudeの判断とは関係なく編集を止める」) echoes the q0 explanation almost word for word, and the item mostly tests hooks versus CLAUDE.md rather than exit codes (o2). Consider rewording the stem so the learner has to use `exit 2` itself, for example by naming in the stem that the hook ends with `exit 2` while the CLAUDE.md line is missing.
summary: Full review after the move to content/courses/claude-code/lessons/: validate 0 errors, lint --strict 0 warnings, est 17.8 min matching estMinutes 18. The biggest strength is the line from worked example to practice: block-rm.sh with predicted manual tests, then a faded protect-files task with layered hints and a 5-item checklist, then a two-candidate evaluation with model write-ups. Every misconception in the brief is corrected in option feedback. No must-fix: the most useful improvements are a content-related distractor for q4 and tying s4's MCP commands and scopes to an objective or a check.
